subject: Follow-up: pricing & continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@retailai.com>, Tom Blake <tom@retailai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & continuous batching assumptions

Thanks again for a productive call earlier today — appreciate the context, Samantha and Tom. Quick recap and next steps so we can get you a clear unit‑economics estimate.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: in‑app assistant for product search & recommendations.
- Expected monthly active users (MAU): ~50k.
- Estimated request frequency: ~1.5 requests/user/day (mix of short prompts and longer completions).
- Average prompt tokens: ~60; average completion tokens: ~290 (rough avg request = ~350 tokens).
- Typical concurrency: steady-state 8–12 concurrency, peak 40–60 during promos.
- Preference for predictable cost and <500ms p50 latency for standard product flows.

What we need from you to finalize an accurate estimate
- Confirm MAU, average requests/day, and any seasonal peaks (you mentioned Black Friday peak planning).
- If possible, export a 7‑day sample of request length distribution (prompt vs completion tokens) — a CSV is perfect.
- Any strict latency SLOs for different routes (search vs conversational flows).

Pricing / Cost topics we'll cover on the estimate
- Baseline compute cost per 1M tokens (raw model inference)
- Continuous batching impact (we typically expect 20–35% token-cost improvement for steady workloads at 8–12 concurrency; more at higher steady concurrency)
- Concurrency/latency tradeoffs and recommended deployment (hosted vs. dedicated)
- Options for reserved capacity and quantization that further lower unit cost

Next steps
1) If you can share a short CSV with token distributions, I’ll loop Marissa and Aditya to produce a short unit‑econ workbook (examples attached).
2) We propose a 30‑minute follow-up next week (Aditya to join) to walk the estimate and pilot options. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed 10:00–12:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood_continuous_batching_assumptions.pdf (short explainer)

Thanks — I’ll hold the proposed slots open.
—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hey Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Below are more concrete numbers from our side that should help your calculations. I attached a short token sample (RetailAI_token_report_Q3.csv).

Key numbers (current estimate)
- MAU: 50,000
- Avg requests per user/day: 1.5
- Avg prompt tokens per request: 60
- Avg completion tokens per request: 290
- Avg tokens per request: ~350
- Monthly requests: 50,000 * 1.5 * 30 ≈ 2.25M requests/month
- Monthly tokens: 2.25M * 350 ≈ 787.5M tokens/month (~788M)

Concurrency / workload shape
- Baseline steady concurrency: ~8–12 (typical daytime usage)
- Peak concurrency (campaigns/promos): 40–60 for short windows (1–4 hours)
- Usage pattern: fairly continuous weekdays 8:00–20:00 PT; lighter overnight and weekends

Target budget / unit economics
- Current internal budget envelope for inference: $8k–$12k/month for this phase (proof of value).
- That implies a target effective cost of roughly $10–$15 per 1M tokens (given ~788M tokens/month) — we know that’s aggressive; want to understand realistic ranges and options (pilot, reserved, quantized models).

SLA notes
- We need p50 < 400ms for standard search flows; p95 can be relaxed to ~900–1200ms for complex completions.

Happy to jump on the follow-up with Aditya & Marissa next week. Tue 11/17 10:30 PT works for Tom and me.

Attachments: RetailAI_token_report_Q3.csv
—
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product, RetailAI

Great — thanks for the CSV and the context, Samantha. Confirming Tue 11/17 10:30 PT for the follow-up.

Internal note / ask to pricing: Marissa/Aditya — please see the usage profile above (approx 788M tokens/mo, steady concurrency 8–12, peaks to 40–60). The customer is targeting ~$10–$15 per 1M tokens for this proof phase. Can you:
- Produce a short unit‑econ workbook showing 3 scenarios: hosted (on‑demand), dedicated reserved (monthly commit), and dedicated + quantization/opt (best case).
- Include an estimate for continuous batching savings (I typically quote 20–35% at these steadies) and sensitivity to steady concurrency (e.g., costs at steady concurrency 6 / 12 / 24).
- Call out likely latency impact at each steady concurrency and recommendations to meet their p50/p95 SLOs.

Customer-facing deliverable: 1‑page summary + one workbook (spreadsheet) showing per‑1M token effective costs and a recommended pilot config. I’ll send the calendar invite for Tue and include the attached redwood assumptions doc as background.

Subject: RE: Follow-up: pricing & continuous batching assumptions

Thanks — quick pricing sketch based on the numbers (assumptions noted inline). I attached a short workbook (RA_unit_econ_estimate.xlsx) with the math.

Assumptions used
- Monthly tokens: 787.5M (from Samantha)
- Avg tokens/request: 350
- Target latency p50: <400ms for search flows; p95 relaxed for completions
- Continuous batching benefit: 30% baseline cost reduction at steady concurrency ~12 (range 20–35% depending on batch fill rate)
- Model baseline compute cost (raw): $15.00 per 1M tokens (example for a high‑capacity decoder model) — this is just the raw inference compute estimate before batching/reservations.

Scenario estimates (effective $ / 1M tokens)
- Hosted on‑demand (no reserved commit): baseline $15.00 -> with continuous batching (30%) => ~$10.50 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated reserved (monthly commit, 20% discount): baseline $12.00 -> with batching => ~$8.40 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated + quantization + reserved (best case): baseline $9.00 -> with batching => ~$6.30 / 1M tokens

Applying to RetailAI volume (~788M tokens/mo)
- Hosted on‑demand: 788 * $10.50 ≈ $8,274 / month
- Dedicated reserved (mid): 788 * $8.40 ≈ $6,619 / month
- Dedicated + quantization (best): 788 * $6.30 ≈ $4,964 / month

Notes / Tradeoffs
- These numbers put RetailAI’s stated budget target ($8k–$12k/month) squarely in the hosted on‑demand range or slightly higher than the dedicated mid scenario; we can meet the target with hosted + batching or with a modest dedicated commit + quantization pilot.
- Peak concurrency (40–60) will require headroom; recommend autoscaling with a small buffer or a burst pool to keep p50 under 400ms during peaks. Continuous batching is most effective for steady, high fill rates; if you see many sub‑100 token requests, batching impact reduces.

Recommended next steps
1) Pilot (2–4 weeks) on hosted with batching enabled and observability (token breakdown, latency by route). We can offer trial credits to cover the pilot run.
2) If PV shows stable steady concurrency and predictable usage, move to a 3‑month reserved capacity commit to get to the dedicated pricing band.
3) Parallel work: ask engineering for a small sample of 1–2k requests (anonymized) to run an internal sim that refines batching improvements and latency estimates.

I’ll bring the workbook to Tue’s call and can walk the per‑1M math line by line.
—
Aditya Rao
